firstDesignDisclosure: THIS IS THE FIRST FINDING-IDENTITY DESIGN IN THE CORPUS. It is not a recovery. No candidate, binding artifact, checker, review, vector or implementation rule found in the measured corpus previously defined how FindingValue.valueDigest or FindingValue.findingId is produced. plan-and-policy-identity-recipes.v2 explicitly declined the question. Every choice labelled AUTHOR-CHOICE below is new and is offered for independent review, not presented as a derivation.
purpose: Propose, in R-1's own successor as freeze section 6 law 19 requires, an exact FINDING-VALUE-DIGEST-V1 recipe for FindingValue.valueDigest and a separate deterministic derivation for FindingValue.findingId. The proposal answers what makes two findings the same for baseline and ratchet purposes, publishes the inclusion and exclusion trades, gives byte-exact vectors, replaces the predecessor's literal-only FindingValue examples with computed values, and names every external input rule that still does not exist. It applies nothing and closes no row.
whatThisDocumentIs: A DELTA. If accepted, the effective v1.7 contract is the duplicate-key-safe parsed value of the pinned v1.6 predecessor with derivedFrom.operations applied in order and nothing else. Every set operation restates the exact predecessor value it replaces. A resolver that finds a different predecessor value must refuse instead of applying the operation.
changesNothing: This lane writes exactly one new file: this one. It edits no reviewed artifact, architecture document, Markdown file, checker, register or predecessor; it repoints no head; it changes no status outside these candidate bytes.

bindingDisclaimer.law19Position: FindingValue is R-1's closed type, so R-1 is the surface entitled to PROPOSE the identity name and domain label. This is the right location and only the right location. Law 19 also says a candidate cannot CLOSE the row; these bytes are CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED, AWAITING-INDEPENDENT-REVIEW, DO-NOT-SEAL, and bind NOTHING.
bindingDisclaimer.noImpliedAcceptance: A correct hash or a green local verification would not apply this design. Exact-byte independent review and an explicit architecture-owner acceptance are still required.
bindingDisclaimer.openDependenciesRemainOpen: The generic hash function is implementable from this file. Production rule-major, typed-subject and canonical-proof-anchor producers are not invented here; they remain the named open dependencies under findingIdentity.openDependencies.
bindingDisclaimer.noOtherVocabularyExtended: No evaluation-proof domain list, D9 vocabulary, fact identity namespace, DELIVERY namespace, baseline schema or rule-IR vocabulary is extended by this candidate.

parseDiscipline.rule: Every JSON document parsed for this design, including these emitted bytes, is decoded through an object_pairs_hook that raises and names a duplicate key. json.loads without that hook is not an admissible parser for this work.
parseDiscipline.classificationRule: Every scalar-leaf classifier tests JSON boolean BEFORE JSON integer. In Python, bool is a subclass of int; integer-first classification is a measured corpus failure mode and is forbidden here.
parseDiscipline.nonFiniteRule: NaN, Infinity and -Infinity are rejected through parse_constant; they are not JSON values and cannot reach identity admission.
parseDiscipline.emittedBytesRule: The finished file must be reparsed under that hook, all recorded counts re-walked from the written value, values patched, and the walk repeated until the complete measurement tuple is unchanged.

forcedByExistingCorpus: R-1 owns FindingValue and therefore owns any namespace and domain label that produces its fields.

FindingValue remains the closed three-field record {ruleId: OpaqueId, findingId: OpaqueId, valueDigest: Digest}; valueDigest has the sha256:<64 lowercase hex> wire type and findingId must satisfy OpaqueId.
The fingerprint is computed host-side from stable rule identity, rule major, typed subject and canonical proof anchor; a rule supplies typed material but does not mint the final fingerprint.
Each fingerprint has one of the recorded stability classes rename-stable, path-stable or span-fallback, and the recipe versions independently of the fact schema.
The host resolves anchors against retained facts and snapshot provenance, rejects fabricated or out-of-scope anchors, canonicalises them, and enforces a per-rule-family closed anchor schema.
Exact-type admission precedes identity derivation; floating point is forbidden; canonical JSON is opensip-canonical-json-v1.
The house digest construction uses SHA-256 over a UTF-8 domain label, one NUL byte, and canonical bytes.

The unchanged v1.6 public core has no entropy or storage input and policy derivation commits findingId; an allocated per-evaluation identifier would destroy deterministic retry equality unless R-1 were rearchitected.
authorChoicesNotDerived: The new recipe name FINDING-VALUE-DIGEST-V1 and domain label opensip.finding-value.v1.
The exact five-field FindingIdentityInputV1 record and CanonicalTypedIdentityV1 wrapper.
Including stabilityClass in the hashed preimage rather than treating it as uncommitted metadata.
Never putting absolute line, column or byte offsets into identity, including in span-fallback; path is admitted only by path-stable and span-fallback typed schemas.
Committing one minimal identity anchor rather than the complete supporting-proof set.
Deriving findingId as the byte-exact string finding: concatenated with valueDigest.
Rejecting duplicate or ambiguous identity material instead of deduplicating, salting, retrying or choosing one.
Repairing the predecessor's literal FindingValue vectors in the effective successor and recomputing every dependent policy-derivation byte field.

productQuestion.question: What makes two findings the same finding?
productQuestion.answer: Under recipe v1, two emissions are the same finding exactly when their admitted FindingIdentityInputV1 values are byte-identical after opensip-canonical-json-v1: the same stable ruleId, the same ruleMajor, the same stabilityClass, the same typed subject (schemaId plus canonical value), and the same typed canonical proof anchor (schemaId plus canonical value). Presentation location, absolute offsets, message, severity, remediation, Run/attempt identities and the complete set of supporting witnesses do not decide sameness.
productQuestion.digestQualification: For storage and comparison, equality is the 32-byte SHA-256 result. If two distinct admitted preimages ever produce one digest in an observation domain where both preimages are available, the host reports a finding-identity integrity fault and accepts neither; it never treats the collision as sameness.
productQuestion.baselineRule: A baseline compares valueDigest only under the exact same declared fingerprint recipe major. Unsupported or mismatched recipe majors are indeterminate, never a mass set of net-new findings. Recipe negotiation and the baseline wire schema remain outside R-1 and are an open dependency rather than invented here.
productQuestion.contentMeaning: Content identity here means the identity-bearing semantic content of a finding, not every display byte. A wording, severity or line-number change does not by itself create a new finding. A change to rule major, typed subject or identity anchor does.

inputSchema.name: FindingIdentityInputV1

ruleId.source: the same verified stable rule identity copied to FindingValue.ruleId

ruleMajor.typeRule: boolean and floating point reject before numeric comparison; the bound reuses R-1's U64 domain
ruleMajor.source: verified rule semantic-major metadata; exact production join is OPEN-DEP-FI-02

stabilityClass.source: host-verified rule-family identity schema classification; exact registry is OPEN-DEP-FI-05

subject.source: host-validated typed subject emitted by evaluation; production schemas are OPEN-DEP-FI-03

canonicalProofAnchor.source: host-resolved and canonicalised minimal identity anchor; production schemas are OPEN-DEP-FI-04

inputSchema.fieldOrderNote: JSON object authoring order carries no identity. opensip-canonical-json-v1 emits keys in its canonical key order; the vectors pin the resulting order canonicalProofAnchor, ruleId, ruleMajor, stabilityClass, subject for the ASCII field names here.

canonicalTypedIdentitySchema.name: CanonicalTypedIdentityV1

schemaId.rule: identifies one closed rule-family-owned subject or identity-anchor schema; changing its meaning in place is forbidden

value.rule: must validate against the closed schema named by schemaId before encoding; all reachable objects are closed and all collection ordering/uniqueness semantics are declared by that schema

canonicalTypedIdentitySchema.whySchemaIdIsInside: Without schemaId, two different typed domains with the same JSON spelling would collide. The corpus requires a TYPED subject and per-rule-family anchor schema; the type identity is therefore identity-bearing.
canonicalTypedIdentitySchema.producerCannotMint: The rule proposes schema-bound material. The host resolves the schema from the admitted rule artifact, validates and canonicalises the value, and computes the digest. A raw producer-supplied canonical string or digest is never authority.

canonicalization.dataModel: objects, arrays, strings, booleans, signed integers and null; floating point forbidden
canonicalization.admissionBeforeEncoding: Duplicate keys, unknown fields, wrong exact scalar types, undeclared collection semantics, invalid schemaId, out-of-scope anchors and non-canonical values reject before a byte is hashed.

undeterminedRegisterChecked.UR-1-key-ordering-plane: The wrapper's keys and every test-schema key in the vectors are ASCII, so scalar/UTF-8/UTF-16 order coincide. Production rule-family schemas MUST use ASCII member names until this corner is settled or name the profile resolution they depend on.
undeterminedRegisterChecked.UR-2-integer-edges: Vectors use only positive integers 1 and 2. ruleMajor is constrained to positive U64. A nested typed schema that requires zero, negative or wider integers inherits the profile's stated rule but has no vector evidence from this candidate.
undeterminedRegisterChecked.UR-3-NFC-action: Admission requires already-NFC strings and rejects non-NFC before encoding. Therefore normalize-versus-reject produces the same bytes for every admitted input and this candidate does not choose between the profile's two surviving readings.
undeterminedRegisterChecked.UR-4-string-escaping: All vector strings are ASCII and need no escape beyond ordinary quotes. Production non-ASCII/control-bearing typed values remain dependent on the authoritative profile text and its independent review; these vectors do not pretend to settle that gap.
undeterminedRegisterChecked.UR-5-lone-surrogates: Rejected before encoding because an admitted NFC Unicode-scalar string cannot contain an unpaired surrogate.

canonicalization.floatRule: No float is ever rounded, stringified or coerced to an integer. It rejects.

rename-stable.promise: The canonical subject and identity anchor do not depend on project-relative path, filename, absolute line, column or byte offset. A file move/rename or unrelated insertion above the evidence leaves the input unchanged.
rename-stable.cost: Requires a semantic or other rename-stable subject and anchor producer. If none exists, the host must use a weaker class or reject; it may not claim rename stability over path material.

path-stable.promise: The typed subject or anchor may include canonical project-relative path but never absolute line, column or byte offsets. Unrelated insertions above the evidence leave identity unchanged; a path rename is allowed to re-identify the finding.
path-stable.cost: Renames report findings as new. The class is honest about that limit and lets baseline tooling explain it rather than silently claiming rename stability.

span-fallback.promise: Used only when no semantic-in-file anchor exists. The typed subject may include canonical path and the identity anchor may include schema-defined matched-span content/context plus an occurrence discriminator, but it still excludes absolute line, column and byte offsets.
span-fallback.cost: A local edit to the matched context or insertion/removal of an indistinguishable occurrence may re-identify the finding. Two indistinguishable occurrences may not be silently collapsed: inability to construct distinct canonical anchors is FINDING_IDENTITY_AMBIGUOUS.

stabilityClasses.noAutomaticUpgrade: Changing stabilityClass changes the preimage. A future stronger subject/anchor recipe requires baseline migration or dual emission; the host never silently relabels a stored digest.

includedFieldTrades.includedValue: stable rule contribution identity, not slug, package coordinate or artifact digest
includedFieldTrades.whatBreaksWhenIncluded: If a publisher incorrectly changes a supposedly rename-stable rule ID, all of that rule's findings re-report. The cost is governed by ContributionId stability.
includedFieldTrades.whatBreaksWhenOmitted: Different rules can produce the same subject/anchor tuple and collide; a baseline entry from one rule can suppress a genuinely different rule.

includedFieldTrades.includedValue: semantic major, not exact rule artifactDigest
includedFieldTrades.whatBreaksWhenIncluded: A major upgrade intentionally re-identifies findings and requires previewable baseline migration or dual emission.
includedFieldTrades.whatBreaksWhenOmitted: A breaking predicate or anchor-semantics change can inherit old suppressions and hide findings the old rule never meant.

includedFieldTrades.standing: CORPUS FORCES RECORDING THE CLASS; HASHING IT IS AUTHOR-CHOICE
includedFieldTrades.whatBreaksWhenIncluded: Improving or weakening the class changes identity even if the schema values happen to serialize the same; migration is required.
includedFieldTrades.whatBreaksWhenOmitted: The same bytes can be compared under incompatible stability promises and a baseline cannot tell whether a rename should preserve identity.

includedFieldTrades.standing: TYPED SUBJECT FORCED; WRAPPER SHAPE AUTHOR-CHOICE
includedFieldTrades.includedValue: one host-validated logical subject under a closed schema
includedFieldTrades.whatBreaksWhenIncluded: Any drift in a subject recipe re-identifies downstream findings; this is why fingerprint recipe support and migrations are user-custody concerns.
includedFieldTrades.whatBreaksWhenOmitted: Two violations of one rule and anchor shape on different logical subjects collide and one can be suppressed. Omitting schemaId also permits cross-type spelling collisions.

includedFieldTrades.standing: CANONICAL PROOF ANCHOR FORCED; MINIMAL IDENTITY-ANCHOR SHAPE AUTHOR-CHOICE
includedFieldTrades.includedValue: the smallest validated anchor key that distinguishes claims on the same subject, not every supporting witness
includedFieldTrades.whatBreaksWhenIncluded: An over-sensitive anchor makes harmless proof rewrites or local refactors look net-new. The rule-family schema must therefore exclude presentation and non-identity witness material.
includedFieldTrades.whatBreaksWhenOmitted: Two genuinely distinct findings from the same rule on the same subject collide. That is the dangerous direction: one can be silently suppressed by a baseline.

excludedFieldTrades.field: absolute line, column, startByte and endByte
excludedFieldTrades.whatBreaksWhenIncluded: An unrelated insertion above a finding changes every later coordinate and re-reports it; ratchet trust collapses.
excludedFieldTrades.whatBreaksWhenOmitted: Repeated identical matches need another discriminator. The rule-family span-context schema supplies one; if it cannot, the host rejects as ambiguous rather than collapsing.

excludedFieldTrades.decision: EXCLUDED FOR rename-stable; CONDITIONALLY INCLUDED inside typed subject/anchor for path-stable and span-fallback; never a universal top-level field
excludedFieldTrades.whatBreaksWhenIncluded: Every rename becomes net-new even when semantic identity is available.
excludedFieldTrades.whatBreaksWhenOmitted: A file-scoped rule with no semantic subject can collide across files. The weaker classes include canonical path honestly when required.

excludedFieldTrades.decision: EXCLUDED; ruleMajor carries intentional semantic breaks
excludedFieldTrades.whatBreaksWhenIncluded: Any implementation-only or wording patch re-reports the rule's complete backlog.
excludedFieldTrades.whatBreaksWhenOmitted: A semantic change shipped without a major bump can inherit suppressions. That is a version-governance defect; exact artifact churn is not an acceptable substitute for semantic versioning.

excludedFieldTrades.field: message, title, severity, remediation, confidence and display excerpts
excludedFieldTrades.whatBreaksWhenIncluded: Copy edits, policy severity changes and redaction/materialisation choices re-identify the finding.
excludedFieldTrades.whatBreaksWhenOmitted: A rule author could change semantics while retaining rule major and identity anchor. Major-version enforcement and rule-family qualification, not display bytes, guard that failure.

excludedFieldTrades.decision: EXCLUDED EXCEPT FOR ONE MINIMAL IDENTITY ANCHOR
excludedFieldTrades.whatBreaksWhenIncluded: Adding a second witness or changing which equivalent fact proves the same claim re-reports the finding.
excludedFieldTrades.whatBreaksWhenOmitted: If the minimal anchor is too small, distinct claims collide. Closed per-rule-family anchor schemas, distinctness qualification and runtime ambiguity rejection guard the dangerous direction.

excludedFieldTrades.field: ProjectId, SnapshotId, PlanId, RequestId, ExecutionId and RunId
excludedFieldTrades.whatBreaksWhenIncluded: The same finding cannot match across deterministic retries, snapshots, runs, project moves or an explicitly imported baseline; lifecycle correlation becomes semantic identity.
excludedFieldTrades.whatBreaksWhenOmitted: A digest can be equal across projects. That is correct for content identity; baseline custody and storage namespaces must scope authority by ProjectId rather than changing the content hash. Cross-project baseline import without provenance remains outside this recipe.

valueDigestRecipe.hash: SHA-256 over the complete preimage; full 256-bit output; truncation forbidden
valueDigestRecipe.output: valueDigest = "sha256:" || lowercase hexadecimal of the 32 digest bytes
valueDigestRecipe.noExtraBytes: No BOM, length prefix, trailing newline, textual preimage hex or outer record is hashed.

findingIdDecision.whyItIsSeparateEvenThoughDerived: valueDigest answers semantic equality. findingId is the typed address/correlation rendering placed in the OpaqueId field. Its v1 mapping is bijective, but the two fields retain different roles and validators.
findingIdDecision.whyDerivedFitsR1: The unchanged evaluate API is pure and deterministic, CoreDeps forbids entropy and storage, and policyDerivationIdentity commits every FindingValue including findingId. Derivation yields byte-identical retries without a registry.
whatDerivedBuys: no CSPRNG, reservation store, collision-retry policy or mutable mapping
same identity across ExecutionId, RequestId and RunId changes
one canonical OpaqueId spelling for each valueDigest
whatDerivedCosts: findingId changes whenever the recipe or any identity-bearing input changes
equality is visible from the identifier
it cannot give two content-identical emissions distinct lifecycle identities; such emissions are either the same finding or an ambiguity defect
whatAllocationWouldBuy: a lifecycle identity that can survive content-recipe migration through an explicit mapping
distinct addresses for otherwise content-identical records
no equality disclosure in the identifier itself
findingIdDecision.whyAllocationIsRejectedHere: Allocation needs CSPRNG bytes, create-new reservation, persistence, collision handling and stable lookup across retries. None is reachable from the closed R-1 evaluate inputs. Fresh allocation would make identical evaluations produce different policy-derivation digests; persistent allocation would introduce a store authority into the pure core. ProjectId is correctly allocated because its owning host surface defines and persists that lifecycle. A FindingValue in this pure return value has the opposite requirements.
findingIdDecision.scopeOfForce: Derived is forced only while preserving the v1.6 R-1 API and deterministic evidence promise. A future R-1 may choose allocation only by explicitly changing those contracts and accepting the storage/lifecycle consequences; this candidate does not claim allocation is universally wrong.

hostComputationOrder: 1. Resolve the admitted rule artifact and stable rule identity; obtain verified ruleMajor. A missing producing join is an open dependency, never guessed from artifactDigest or a version-looking string.
2. Receive the rule's typed subject and proposed identity anchor material. Resolve every anchor reference against retained facts and snapshot provenance; reject fabricated or out-of-scope material.

3. Resolve the closed schemas named by subject.schemaId and canonicalProofAnchor.schemaId from the admitted rule family. Validate exact types, closure, ordering, uniqueness and stability-class eligibility.
4. Build the closed FindingIdentityInputV1. Reject non-NFC input, floats, duplicate keys and every canonical-json-profile corner the admitted schema cannot settle.
5. Compute canonical bytes, prepend the 24 domain bytes and one 0x00 byte, SHA-256 the full preimage, and render valueDigest.
6. Derive findingId by prefixing the complete valueDigest with finding:. Copy the verified ruleId into FindingValue.
7. Before accepting the rule partition, enforce duplicate, ambiguity and digest-collision rules over all emitted findings. Then order FindingList under the inherited R-1 orderRule.

ambiguityAndCollisionRules.duplicateEmission: Two emissions with byte-identical admitted FindingIdentityInputV1 in one rule partition are a duplicate rule output. Reject the partition as FINDING_IDENTITY_DUPLICATE; do not silently deduplicate.
ambiguityAndCollisionRules.ambiguousProjection: Two distinct resolved subject/anchor source tuples that a rule-family projection maps to one canonical FindingIdentityInputV1 are FINDING_IDENTITY_AMBIGUOUS. Reject the partition; the anchor schema is too weak.
ambiguityAndCollisionRules.sha256Collision: One valueDigest observed for two different canonical preimage byte strings is FINDING_IDENTITY_COLLISION, a host integrity fault. Reject both; never salt, retry, select one or allocate a replacement ID.
ambiguityAndCollisionRules.suppliedMismatch: A supplied or persisted valueDigest or findingId is never authority. Recompute both; malformed text rejects as representation error and well-formed inequality rejects as FINDING_IDENTITY_MISMATCH.
ambiguityAndCollisionRules.ruleIdMismatch: FindingValue.ruleId unequal to the identity input and admitted rule is FINDING_IDENTITY_RULE_MISMATCH.
ambiguityAndCollisionRules.d9Boundary: These are internal R-1 design names only. This candidate does not assign a D9 class, public error code or exit status; D9 owns that projection.

openDependencies.missing: A binding join from R-1 RuleValue.ruleId to the architecture's rename-stable ContributionId for the exact admitted rule.
openDependencies.whyNotChosen: R-1 types ruleId only as OpaqueId and the sweep classifies it LITERAL-ONLY. Treating a slug, package coordinate or arbitrary rule-emitted text as the stable ID would invent the most important preimage field.
openDependencies.implementationPosture: The generic identity function accepts a verified ruleId. Production evaluation rejects if the host cannot supply the verified join.

openDependencies.missing: A producing rule for ruleMajor reachable by the pure core.
openDependencies.whyNotChosen: The string ruleMajor occurs in architecture/02's formula and nowhere in the JSON contract corpus. RuleValue carries ruleId and artifactDigest only. Parsing an arbitrary contributionVersion or substituting artifactDigest would be invention and would have opposite baseline behavior.
openDependencies.implementationPosture: Implement the field and vectors; do not ship a production rule until the owning rule/plan surface binds its source or an R-1 successor lawfully extends the input shape.

openDependencies.missing: Closed production typed-subject schemas plus deterministic mappings from admitted facts/rule output to their CanonicalTypedIdentityV1 values.
openDependencies.whyNotChosen: Fact-plane SubjectIdV1 is a grammar, not one universal subject producer, and the corpus records a live divergence between fact-plane namespaced subjects and path-like evaluation-proof subjects. Choosing one here would decide another surface's unresolved vocabulary.
openDependencies.implementationPosture: test:* schemas are vectors only. Unknown production schemaId rejects.

openDependencies.missing: Per-rule-family canonical identity-anchor schemas and projection rules, including context/occurrence discrimination for repeated span fallback findings.
openDependencies.whyNotChosen: Fact anchor records carry SnapshotId, path and absolute byte bounds and therefore cannot be hashed verbatim without making line shifts and renames churn. No artifact defines the smaller identity anchor. This candidate specifies its required properties but does not manufacture rule-family keys.
openDependencies.implementationPosture: Resolve and validate anchors; reject a rule whose admitted family has no identity-anchor schema or whose projection is ambiguous.

openDependencies.missing: A binding registry joining each production subject/anchor schema pair to one stabilityClass and qualification corpus.
openDependencies.whyNotChosen: The three class names are sealed, but no artifact says which real schema earns which promise. A label without rename/line-shift controls would be an assertion, not stability evidence.
openDependencies.implementationPosture: A test fixture may declare its class. Production admission rejects an unregistered pair.

openDependencies.missing: A full durable Finding/baseline schema that visibly stores fingerprint recipe major, stabilityClass and recomputable identity material or a content-addressed reference to it.
openDependencies.whyNotChosen: R-1 FindingValue has exactly three fields. Hashing stabilityClass commits it but does not make the class inspectable. Architecture requires baselines to declare recipe version, and no artifact defines that Finding schema. Adding fields outside R-1's narrow completion value or designing baseline custody here would exceed R-1 authority.
openDependencies.implementationPosture: crates/core can compute and return both required fields. A durable baseline feature remains indeterminate until its owning surface binds the visible metadata and compatibility protocol.

openDependencies.missing: Canonical-json profile closure for any production schema that needs an UNDETERMINED corner, especially non-ASCII key ordering or non-ASCII/control string escaping vectors.
openDependencies.whyNotChosen: canonical-json-profile.v1 records those corners rather than choosing them. This candidate's vectors deliberately avoid them and cannot upgrade prose-stated rules into vector-forced facts.
openDependencies.implementationPosture: Use the authoritative profile text, constrain admitted schemas as stated above, and do not claim byte qualification for an unexercised corner.

implementationBoundary.canBeImplementedNow: A crates/core finding_identity module can validate the closed generic input, canonicalize it, compute valueDigest, derive findingId, verify all seven vectors byte-exactly, replace the inherited synthetic finding, and recompute the affected policy-derivation values.
implementationBoundary.cannotBeClaimedYet: The current corpus cannot produce every generic input from a real admitted rule because OPEN-DEP-FI-01 through OPEN-DEP-FI-05 are unresolved, and it cannot persist a baseline-complete Finding because OPEN-DEP-FI-06 is unresolved. This candidate refuses to turn those absences into author choices.
implementationBoundary.firstCommitOutcome: The core crate is no longer blocked on the hash function or either output-field algorithm. Its production integration remains fail-closed at the named joins rather than accepting literals.

strongestObjectionsExpected: The minimal identity-anchor abstraction may simply move the hard collision problem into per-rule schemas. That is true; the response is explicit schema ownership, qualification and runtime ambiguity rejection, not a claim that SHA-256 solves semantic identity.
Including stabilityClass makes an upgrade churn identity. Omitting it permits cross-class comparison under a false promise. This candidate chooses explicit migration over ambiguous equality.

Derived findingId duplicates valueDigest information. It is intentional type/address redundancy forced by the unchanged three-field R-1 shape; allocation would introduce unavailable authority and nondeterminism.

Excluding absolute offsets can make repeated identical spans hard to distinguish. The candidate chooses a visible failure over silent suppression: if context plus occurrence cannot distinguish them, evaluation is ambiguous and not a valid finding set.

The generic function is implementable while real producers remain open. This is narrower than full blocker closure and is stated as such; inventing ruleMajor or production anchor schemas to claim more would violate the task's dependency rule.
